text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Hundreds of Ogoni youths to benefit from job skills acquisition programme launched by Shell Nigeria unit.

- Oil marketing companies' inability to lift fuel from the depots is responsible for the lingering fuel shortages nationwide, Mohammed Jubrilla, media relations manager of state-run oil company NNPC, says.

- Chief executive officer of oil marketing company Mobil Producing Unlimited Daniel Deubreuilly says his company has concluded plans to introduce new generation of automotive lubricants into the market from September.
- Fire in Echeno village, central Kogi state, renders about 3,000 people homeless and destroys properties worth several millions of naira.
- Some commercial banks seek approval from regulator Central Bank to shut down branches considered unviable in attempt to curb further financial losses.
- Former Nigerian ruler Shehu Shagari intervenes in the long-running leadership tussle in Democratic Party of Nigeria, one of five registered political parties.

- Traditional ruler of southeastern town Bonny, construction site of the $4 billion liquefied natural gas plant, gives pledge to government that his people will ensure protection of the installations and workers there.
